Plot S3 method for coverage data

Source: R/plot.cd_coverage_selected.R
plot.cd_coverage_selected.Rd

Draws the latest coverage of a set of indicators. National data, or the data of one region, is drawn as a profile (bars by indicator and source) or as the gap between the facility and the survey estimate. Subnational data is drawn as dots by unit, one panel per indicator, or as a heatmap of units by indicator.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cd_coverage_selected'
plot(
  x,
  type = NULL,
  source_labels = NULL,
  indicator_labels = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  x_title = NULL,
  y_title = NULL,
  legend_title = NULL,
  ...,
  options = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An object of class cd_coverage_selected.

type

"profile" or "gap" (for national), "dot" or "heatmap" (for subnational).

source_labels

(Optional) Named list to translate 'facility', 'survey', 'wuenic'.

indicator_labels

(Optional) Named list to translate indicator names (e.g. 'anc4').

title

The chart's title.

subtitle

The line under the title.

caption

The note under the chart.

x_title

The title of the horizontal axis.

y_title

The title of the vertical axis.

legend_title

The title of the legend.

...

Chart options by name (see cd_chart_options()): background, fonts, sizes, axes, grid, legend, colours. Other arguments are ignored.

options

A cd_chart_options() object or a list of chart options: a look made once, to give to several charts. Applied after the text arguments, so a text it holds wins over them.

Value

A ggplot object with the chart options applied. Which chart it is depends on type and on the admin level of x.

Examples

cache <- load_cache_data(system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core"))
#> ℹ Loading Excel "kenya.xlsx" for parts
#> ! The following columns are empty: anc_1trimester, under5_deaths, total_deaths,
#>   ipv2, measles_cases
#> ℹ Successfully loaded and cleaned data
#> ℹ Auto-detect candidates (|group|): vaccine=19, rmncah=28 -> selected rmncah
cache$set_national_estimates(list(sbr = 0.02))
cache$adjust_data()

# national: a profile of the indicators, or the gap between facility data and the survey
national <- cache$generate_coverage_data("national", "maternal")
plot(national, type = "profile")

plot(national, type = "gap", title = "Facility data against the survey", legend_position = "bottom")
#> Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range
#> (`geom_segment()`).
#> Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range
#> (`geom_point()`).


# by region: a heatmap (or "dot")
regions <- cache$generate_coverage_data("adminlevel_1", "child")
plot(regions, type = "heatmap", legend_title = "Coverage (%)")
